newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes steady against firm outrights.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes steady against firm outrights.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes continued on a steady course heading to the later stages of Friday business, attracting dwindling attention for May barrels.
Cash traders said the market has been dulled by today's pipeline scheduling day and a lack of emphasis for June barrels.
Current prices put June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing around 5 cents higher at $20.00-10 a barrel. The May/June WTI roll has stayed between 15-20 cts in favor of the May.
Gains for June WTI came on Shell saying it would reduce Nigerian Forcados output due to continuing ethnic conflicts.
Grade business focused on Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James, which steadied at a 20 cts premium to May WTI/Cushing. June LLS was charted around a 5-10 cts discount to the marker.
Midland/WTI was last done for May at WTI/Cushing -38 cts, with the June month selling at a 30 cts discount.
May West Texas Sour/Midland was sold at $1.45 under the marker, some 15 cts stronger than Thursday. Traders said volumes were very thin.
May WTI/Cushing Postings hovered around last deals at $1.56 and $1.57, traders said.

Much of the bullish tint noted late Thursday for outright prices was deflated earlier in the session after United Nations officials denied a BBC monitoring service report that oil monitors went missing in northern Iraq.
